column1: # THE LAYERING (CLAUDE.md, Design rules; project/Coupling.scala `Layers`, `sbt couplingReport`, scripts/coupling-report):
# every production package's layer, bottom (0) up, and inside an ORDERED layer (the application's, 3, and the composition
# roots', 5) every package's rank, bottom (0) up. A package may depend only on its own layer or a lower one, and inside
# an ordered layer only on its own rank or a lower one. The coupling ratchet (scripts/ci/coupling_ratchet.py) fails on
# any package edge into a higher layer or a higher rank (naming the direction allowed), on a package no `layer` row
# places, on a package of an ordered layer with no `rank` row -- a new package takes its place here in the commit that
# adds it -- and on any package cycle at all (no row, no trailer excuses one). Loosening the table -- an `allow` row
# added, a package given another layer or rank -- lands only in a commit carrying `Coupling: <why>` (the ratchet checks
#   layer<TAB><n><TAB><package prefix><TAB><why it sits there>   the longest prefix naming a package decides
#   rank<TAB><n><TAB><package><TAB><why it sits there>          the package itself (never a prefix), inside its layer
#   allow<TAB><from>-><to><TAB><why>                          an upward edge kept on purpose (keep this list short)
# The ranks are the package graph's order, written down (2026-11-18: the last two cycles cut, 0 left): an edge that would
# close a cycle is an upward edge first. To cut one: move the type to the package its users sit on, or one rank down,
# or put a small trait in the lower package. Packages of one rank may use each other only one way (no cycle).
